newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia sets tough terms for Surgut Holding stake.
newsitem.headline: Russia sets tough terms for Surgut Holding stake.

text.p: Bidders for a 40.12 percent stake in Russian oil company NK Surgutneftegaz (Surgut Holding) will have to offer at least 410 billion roubles ($72.9 million) for the shares and 1.2 trillion roubles in investment, the Federal Property Fund said on Tuesday.
The winner will also have to transfer five percent of Surgut Holding's main operating company, AO Surgutneftegaz to Surgut Holding, it said in the latest edition of its Reforma bulletin.

The winner must transfer the 1.2 trillion roubles in company investment within three months of winning the auction and must pay another 100 billion roubles for social services in the region of Surgut headquarters within a year.
The Federal Property Fund is selling the four-million-share stake currently held in trust by Surgut Holding's pension fund under the government's shares-for-loans scheme.
Surgut Holding is one of a dozen or so vertically-integrated Russian oil groups created over the last few years.

The pension fund won the stake in Surgut Holding in November 1995 in the first transaction under the controversial shares-for-loans scheme, in which investors won the right to manage state-owned shares in partly privatised companies in return for loans to the government.
The pension fund is in turn mostly owned by Surgut Holding.
Next month's auction to transfer ownership of the stake will be the third such sale of stakes acquired in shares-for-loans deals, following auctions of stakes in oil groups YUKOS and SIDANKO.
In both these cases the auctions were won by companies which according to analysts appear to have close links with those who won the original shares-for-loans contests.
